clue.text: Warning sign of Tory describing far-right group

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the Tories are the party of the political right
the EDL, English Defence League, is a British far-right street movement

explanation.surface: A warning about a Conservative politician's links with an extremist organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory' stands for the political right. The English Defence League is a British far-right street movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A red traffic signal or lamp is the standard signal telling people to stop because of danger.

clue.text: Bank charge right to go up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A bank's charge is set to increase, rightly or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go up' reverses FEE plus R, read upwards in the grid. 'Bank' wants to be a lender with charges; it is a sandbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or sand near the water's surface, a kind of bank.

clue.text: See daughter's worried

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees
ate is the past of eat in the sense of worry, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A parent notices that their girl is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE uses 'eat' meaning to worry or trouble someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing someone romantically means going out with them, dating them.

clue.text: I travel across north on bypass

indicators.note: one piece lies across the other, so the second sits within the first

parts.note: to go is to travel
re means on or concerning, as in letters

explanation.surface: A driver crosses northwards using the ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' signals the insertion of north; 'on' is the crossword staple meaning 'regarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go around it, to pass it by and disregard it.

clue.text: Mo Farah hasn't primarily lost races like these

definitions.text: Mo Farah hasn't primarily lost races like these

indicators.note: races suggests letters charging around the track and ending up in a new order
primarily means first, so the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Mo Farah has rarely been beaten over this distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes L from 'lost' and 'races' stirs it in with MO FARAH HASNT; the whole clue is also the definition. Mo Farah is a British Olympic distance-running champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Half marathons are road races over about 13.1 miles, an event Farah mostly won, so the sentence describes them truly.

clue.text: Stretches out with small steps

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
paces are strides or steps taken in walking

explanation.surface: Someone walks with short strides to stretch their legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To space things is to set them at intervals, spreading or stretching them along a line.

clue.text: Delight as extremes of arachnophobia treated with spider

indicators.note: something treated is processed or altered, so the letters are reworked
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fear of spiders is cured by exposure to a spider, to the patient's delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes A and A from 'arachnophobia'; 'treated' mixes them with SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a state of perfect happiness or bliss, sheer delight.

clue.text: Catching two rings separately in act using juggling

indicators.note: juggling tosses things about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O, so two rings give two Os

explanation.surface: A circus act involving two rings being juggled proves infectious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'juggling' rearranges ACT USING; 'separately in' says each O sits apart inside it, which the full shuffle of all ten letters also gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious illness is one that is caught by contact, so catching means the same.

clue.text: Nuts about prince: princess gets tear on the frosty circuit?

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other, surrounding it

parts.note: nuts are a kind of seeds
Kate, the Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A royal tabloid picture: a crazy prince and a princess in tears on an icy course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' looks like crying; it is the verb meaning to race. KATE is Catherine, Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed-skate is to race fast on ice, so tearing round an icy track fits; the question mark flags the playful wording.

clue.text: Caught up in nasty net, fish died

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad, twisted state, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A creature is snared in a cruel net and the fish perishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' turns NET into ENT; ANGLE is the verb 'fish', not a kind of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entangled means being snarled or caught up in something, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Round opening of this: is Tesco worried?

definitions.text: Round opening of this: is Tesco worried?

indicators.note: worried means harassed and shaken up, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Is the supermarket chain Tesco anxious about a rival bargain shop opening nearby?
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' takes T from 'this'; 'worried' rearranges ROUND, T and IS TESCO. Tesco is Britain's biggest supermarket chain, threatened by budget rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget shop selling goods cheaply is what would worry a big grocer when a new one opens around the corner.

clue.text: Variety of fruit that's peeled

indicators.note: peeling a fruit takes off its skin, here the outer letters of the word

parts.note: oranges are citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A kind of fruit sold with its skin already removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' strips O and S, the outer letters of ORANGES; the fruit is plural, which a solver trying ORANGE misses.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is an assortment or variety, as in a wide range of goods.

clue.text: Spiderman spinning with old 6

indicators.note: spinning sets the letters whirling into a new order, apt for a web-spinner

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The superhero whirls around with an old friend, as if in a comic strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 refers to the answer at 6-down, PARADISE. 'spinning' rearranges SPIDERMAN plus OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The land promised to Abraham's descendants has become a byword for an ideal place of bliss, as heaven is.

clue.text: Struggled and sank when crossing lake

indicators.note: crossing a thing means straddling it, so one piece spans the other

parts.note: a ship that foundered sank
L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A swimmer struggled and went under while attempting to cross a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when crossing' puts L inside FOUNDERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to thrash about clumsily, struggling to make progress.

clue.text: Soldiers on a hard section

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
severe means hard or harsh

explanation.surface: Infantry advance over a difficult stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' wants to be troops; it is the verb, as in 'soldiers on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to keep going despite difficulty, which is to persist.

clue.text: Song told a tale

definitions.meaning: a German art song, as composed by Schubert or Schumann
telling a tale is lying, saying something untrue

explanation.surface: A ballad that narrated a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for a song is used in English for a classical art song, and the verb sense is having spoken falsely.

clue.text: Hear which method of transport British 5 select

definitions.note: heard aloud, which becomes witch, so this means a witch's way of travelling

parts.note: the answer at 5-across, SPACES; rooms are spaces, as in room to move
to tick an option on a form is to select it

explanation.surface: A question about which British transport option to choose, as on a form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear which' is a sound-alike trick inside the definition: it says WITCH, so the definition is a witch's method of transport. 5 points to SPACES, which are ROOMS.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a witch flies on a besom, the long-handled brush she rides through the night sky.

clue.text: Comforts one son after do

indicators.note: the later pieces come after the first in the answer

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them
sole means one and only

explanation.surface: A parent soothes their child after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a party; it is the verb meaning to cheat, CON.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to comfort them in distress.

clue.text: Not decent, wearing one at the front

indicators.note: the word for one is placed at the head of the other piece

parts.note: un is French for one
sporting something is wearing it proudly, as in sporting a tie

explanation.surface: Wearing a single garment up front is judged indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is French here, and 'wearing' is used in the sense of showing off a garment, as in sporting a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsporting behaviour is unfair play, not what a decent, fair-minded person would do.

clue.text: Place tee for golf shot

parts.note: to put something is to place it
the letter T is pronounced and spelt as tee

explanation.surface: A golfer sets a ball on its peg before hitting.
explanation.walkthrough: A tee is used for drives, so the surface points away from the gentle stroke on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A putt is the light stroke played on the green to roll the ball towards the hole.

clue.text: Quite old clothes on

indicators.note: to clothe something is to cover it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: aged means old
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Elderly people wearing their old clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is the verb meaning wraps, not garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying Quite! as a reply means you concur, the same as replying that you are in accord.

clue.text: Slash department, then recruit

parts.note: a division is a section or department of an organisation
to sign a player or employee is to recruit them

explanation.surface: A manager cuts one department, then hires new staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slash' looks like a verb about cutting the department; it is the noun for the stroke '/'.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward stroke character can stand for division in arithmetic, as in 6/3.

clue.text: Nothing on sides of coffee mug

parts.note: FA, short for sweet Fanny Adams, is British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A coffee mug with nothing on its sides, plain and undecorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides of' takes C and E from 'coffee'. Sweet FA is British slang for nothing. 'mug' is slang for the face, not a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is slang for a person's face, as in an ugly mug.

clue.text: Story in bed

definitions.meaning: the storyline or narrative of a novel or film
a garden bed, a small patch of ground for growing plants

explanation.surface: A bedtime tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The storyline of a book is its narrative, and a small patch of earth planted with vegetables is a garden bed.

clue.text: Start to register web address blocked by one country

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
something blocked by another has it lodged within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a URL is a web address
a means one, as in a dog

explanation.surface: Signing up begins with a web address, but one entry gets in the way for a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' takes R from 'register'; 'blocked by' puts A inside URL.
explanation.definitionFit: Country used as an adjective, as in country life, describes the countryside, the opposite of urban.

clue.text: Nearly finish novel, then complete block

indicators.note: nearly a word means most of it, with its last letter lost

parts.note: to stop is to finish
novel means new
all means complete, the whole

explanation.surface: A writer almost finishes a book, then hits writer's block entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the last letter of STOP to leave STO. 'novel' looks like a book but is the adjective NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to obstruct by stalling or refusing to answer, blocking progress.

clue.text: Stop in dodgy side street

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or shifty, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A warning to halt in a shady back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges SIDE into DESI.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or refrain from doing something.

clue.text: When there's nothing between leading couple, no more passion

definitions.text: When there's nothing between leading couple

parts.note: something no more has ceased to be, it is dead
heat is ardour or passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: Romance dies when a lead couple has nothing left between them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a sad romance, but 'nothing between leading couple' is two front-runners tied.
explanation.definitionFit: A race tie happens when the first two finishers cannot be separated, with no gap at all between them.
